title: Fast Recovery Capacity Gambit — SLO Ops Notes
body:
Purpose:
Drive a short, pragmatic cross-functional program to protect SLOs during partial regional outages or sudden capacity pressure for model-serving traffic. The gambit: short-term targeted capacity expansion + graceful degradation policies + curated routing fallbacks to preserve user-visible latency and error-rate SLOs while minimizing long-term cost and blast-radius.

Context / why this exists (notes to self):
- We repeatedly see spikes where model-serving tails cause large token-latency variance across customers. Existing fallback rules are conservative and sometimes route to expensive hosted variants too late.
- We need a repeatable, low-friction playbook that product, platform, infra, SRE and solutions-eng can run with 1–2 hours notice.
- This doc is intentionally operational and pragmatic — not an academic SLO design doc.

Scope (in-scope):
- Model-serving endpoints (hosted + dedicated) for text generation and chat with per-route SLOs (p99 latency, error-rate).
- Cross-region traffic shaping and region-fallbacks.
- Autoscale/spot-burst playbooks for Dedicated pools.
- Observability signals and runbook triggers.

Scope (out-of-scope):
- Long-term capacity architecture redesigns (separate project).
- Billing implications beyond immediate guardrails (finance review separate).

Key stakeholders and roles (working names):
- Program lead / incident coordinator: Aisha Patel (SRE) — run decisions, comms.
- Serving runtime lead: Miguel Santos — implement route-level throttles and kernel fallbacks.
- Platform / infra: Evelyn Park — capacity ops (provision burst nodes, scale pools).
- Product / feature owner: Priya Ramesh — evaluate customer impact & prioritize protected routes.
- Solutions / CS liaison: Liam O'Connor — coordinate customer-facing comms and opt-ins.
- Security & compliance support: Zara Nguyen — ensure emergency fallbacks comply with data residency/KMS rules.

High-level gambit mechanics (operational summary):
1) Detect pre-failure window via signal combination: queue growth + p95 latency drift + scheduler tail busy.
2) Open emergency decision channel (SRE bridge + platform slack channel + product PM).
3) If thresholds met, execute capacity gambit: provision N hot nodes or reserve burst capacity in Dedicated and flip smart-routing to prefer low-latency replicas for critical routes.
4) Apply short-lived model variant fallbacks on non-critical routes (lower-cost quantized variants or reduced max_tokens) to free KV cache and kernel resources.
5) Deploy gradual client-facing throttles for non-protected buckets (best-effort) to maintain overall cluster health.
6) Monitor for 30–120 minutes, validate SLO recovery; if stable, slowly retract burst capacity and restore normal route policies.

Decision thresholds and triggers (draft):
- Trigger A (notice): sustained 3-minute p95 latency > baseline + 30% AND queue size > 2x normal for 5 minutes.
- Trigger B (action): p99 latency exceeds SLO by > 20% for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows OR error-rate spike > 1% absolute on customer-critical routes.
- Manual escalation: product requests protection for named customers (via PM) even below thresholds.

50-day tactical plan (milestones and owners):
- Day 0–7: Finalize decision thresholds and alert playbook (owner: Aisha).
- Day 8–18: Implement programmatic routing flip and short-lived policy API (owner: Miguel).
- Day 19–28: Add Dedicated burst orchestration runbooks (Evelyn).
- Day 29–36: Create protected-route registry and opt-in customer list (Priya + Liam).
- Day 37–44: Run two tabletop exercises with oncall (SRE) + platform + product; iterate on timing and comms cadence (all).
- Day 45–50: Soft launch: run gambit in controlled capacity-sim tests and measure rollback friction (all).

Success criteria / metrics to watch (primary):
- Protected routes: p99 latency returns within SLO bounds within 10 minutes of gambit execution in >= 80% of incidents.
- Error rate on protected routes: no increase > 0.5% absolute during gambit in >= 90% of runs.
- Time to rollback: median retract time < 25 minutes after stable signals.
- Cost guardrail: incremental burst cost capped at configurable delta (TBD) per activation, with finance alert if exceeded.

Runbook excerpt (quick checklist):
1) Open incident bridge and tag with label "capacity-gambit".
2) Confirm triggers using runbook dashboard (link below). If unsure, default to manual review with PM.
3) Execute "provision-burst" script (infra credentials required). Monitor instance health.
4) Toggle routing policy to "protected-mode" for list-of-routes (via policy API).
5) Apply temporary throttles for non-protected traffic using rate-limiter keys.
6) Observe metrics for 5, 15, 30 min windows. If p99 still high after 30 min, escalate to exec recovery call.
7) When stable, reverse toggles: ramp down throttles, remove burst nodes with graceful drain.

Observability & dashboards (what to build):
- Capacity gambit dashboard (single pane): cluster queue length, p50/95/99 for protected routes, error-rate per-route, instance utilization, allocated burst costs (est).
- Alert groups: trigger A (notice), trigger B (action). Include clear runbook link in alert.

Comms cadence & templates (for SRE/Platform/Product teams):
- Immediate: Bridge summary + short description, time, and actions requested.
- 15-min update: health metrics + whether rollback planned.
- Post-incident: 1–2 pager to stakeholders with timeline, impact, decisions, follow-ups.

Customer comms play (if public-facing issue):
- Liaise with Solutions/CS (Liam) to identify customers that require proactive outreach.
- Draft status updates and pin to status.redwood.ai if multi-hour impact.

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Burst capacity provisioning fails under cloud quotas. Mitigation: maintain warm reserve pools and run monthly reserve tests.
- Risk: Temporary fallbacks degrade output quality for customers. Mitigation: protect a minimum set of customers/routes and include quality regression test as part of tabletop.
- Risk: Cost blowouts from repeated activations. Mitigation: rate-limit activations per 24-hour window and finance alerts.

Unresolved questions / open decisions (to surface in next working session):
- Exact finance cost cap for a single activation (proposal: $Xk/day — need finance input).
- How many protected routes (and how to rank them)? Build a tiered registry (P0/P1/P2) with PM input.
- Data residency: can we spin burst nodes in different regions for certain customers? Security check needed.

Short-term action items (next 7 days):
- Aisha: final draft of alert thresholds and add to alerting triage board.
- Miguel: prototype policy flip API with mock toggles.
- Evelyn: list of possible Dedicated clusters that can support burst and run quota checks.
- Priya: draft protected-route candidate list and customer impact notes.
- Liam: prepare customer comms template.

Appendix: useful links & artifacts
- Quick runbook dashboard: (internal) https://metrics.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity-gambit
- Confluence primer for SLO tiers: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Tiering
- Incident runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Runbook+Template

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the gambit simple; we will overcomplicate if we try to automate all edge-cases up front.
- Tabletop is priority — nothing exposes gaps faster than a 90-minute simulated pressure test.
- Remember to include product in the 15-min cadence for customer-impact tradeoffs.

-- end of doc --
